name: Patanjali Foods Ltd
title: Patanjali Foods Ltd - 500368 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Patanjali Foods Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR11,156 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.48% and FY27 guidance points to 12-15% blended EBITDA growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue from operations at INR11,155.60 crore, with EBITDA excluding exceptional items of INR501.96 crore (4.48% margin) and PBT of INR235.69 crore (2.10% margin). FY26, the first full year after the HPC business integration, delivered revenue of INR40,169.58 crore, crossing the INR40,000 crore mark, with EBITDA of INR1,931.52 crore (4.79%). Edible oil and FMCG grew double digits, while staples (rice) and ghee softened sequentially in Q4. Management flagged a sharp crude-linked edible oil price spike from March 2026 and a further rise in April, which it expects to be beneficial to large players in the near term.

segments.name: Edible oil
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR8,324 crore (+23.28% YoY), EBITDA margin 2.58%; branded oil about 75% of edible oil sales. Edible oil volume 20.3 lakh tonnes vs 18.84 lakh tonnes last year; aggregate segment volume 25.1 lakh tonnes vs 23.64 lakh tonnes.

segments.name: FMCG (Foods + HPC)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR2,890 crore (25.76% of revenue) with 57.62% of EBITDA; FY26 revenue INR11,188 crore (+19.95%), EBITDA margin 10.81%.

segments.name: Biscuits
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR477.89 crore (+13.97% YoY), slightly down QoQ from INR490 crore in Q3; FY26 INR1,907.81 crore (+15.9%), highest ever. Doodh biscuits FY26 turnover over INR1,300 crore vs INR1,000 crore in FY25. Q4 EBITDA INR65 crore.

segments.name: Staples and ghee
segments.commentary: Staples Q4 revenue INR848.83 crore, FY26 INR3,658 crore; sequential drop of about INR407 crore driven mainly by rice. Ghee Q4 INR338.91 crore, FY26 INR1,423.86 crore; ghee sales fell about INR129 crore on early-summer and Middle East disruption. Staples Q4 EBITDA INR5.46 crore.

segments.name: Ethnic foods (Foods business)
segments.commentary: Foods business Q4 EBITDA INR72 crore combined, of which ethnic foods INR66 crore and staples INR5.46 crore. Mid-teens YoY decline was flagged by an analyst; management did not dispute the figure.

segments.name: Nutrela (soya/textured)
segments.commentary: Nutrela Q4 revenue INR106 crore, FY26 INR527 crore; Q4 EBITDA INR16.85 crore. Textured soya FY26 revenue INR526.78 crore.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR17.94 crore, FY26 INR58 crore after portfolio rationalisation; Q4 EBITDA INR2 crore.

segments.name: Home and Personal Care (HPC)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR840.50 crore (+35.42% YoY), EBITDA INR136 crore. Dental INR425.97 crore in Q4 and INR1,412.80 crore in FY26; skin care INR239.75 crore in Q4 (+57.66% YoY), FY26 INR680 crore; home care INR97.82 crore in Q4, FY26 INR331.88 crore.

segments.name: Oil palm plantation
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,793 crore and EBITDA INR357 crore vs INR203 crore prior year, helped by maturing plantations and higher palm oil prices. Cultivated area 1,10,722 hectares as of 31 March 2026, +23.65% YoY; about 38% in the 7-25 year prime yielding phase.

guidance_outlook: Edible oil volume growth of about 3-5% in FY27, in line with expected national consumption growth; management said it is slightly below 4%.
Foods portfolio revenue growth of 8-10% on a blended basis in FY27, with Foods margins expected to recover to about 10% after FY26 softness.
HPC revenue growth target of about 15% in FY27, with EBITDA margin near or above 18%, about 200 bps better than under the parent.
Blended EBITDA growth of 12-15% expected in FY27.
Edible oil EBITDA maintained in a 2-4% range despite near-term price volatility.
Q1 and Q2 FY27 expected to be very positive for edible oil and oilseed crushing, given Indonesian export-centralisation disruption.
Biscuit target of high double-digit growth, with Q1 FY27 expected to show a substantial uptick from INR478 crore in Q4 FY26.
capex_capacity: Oil palm cultivated area 1,10,722 hectares at 31 March 2026, +23.65% YoY and +2,558 hectares QoQ; total allocated area 6.63 lakh hectares.
Oil palm production fell in Q4 FY26 due to seasonality, while maturing plantations are expected to drive volume growth.
No new capex or commissioning timelines were given in the call.
demand_pricing: Palm, soyabean and sunflower oil prices rose about 20%, 23% and 22% respectively between January and March 2026 (RBD palm, refined soy and sunflower, per prepared remarks); April 2026 YoY increases were palm 15%, soybean 17%, sunflower 22%.
Consumer shift toward mustard oil observed as palm-linked prices rose; mustard, groundnut and cottonseed are domestic oils.
Edible oil price hikes were passed through almost daily; management said prices rose 10-15% (about 14% overall) and that its prices moved in line with the market.
Staples and ghee price hikes of 2-5% taken; ethnic foods other than ghee largely not repriced. Pulses and rice also repriced.
Cost of goods sold rose 98 bps QoQ and 294 bps YoY in Q4 FY26, with pressure from packaging, freight and insurance after mid-March.
Receivable days rose; INR700-800 crore of extra credit extended to customers. Advances paid to vendors for raw material security raised borrowings.
Rice category demand declined substantially through FY26; drought/El Nino and government policy risks flagged for staples.
Retail inflation 3.4% in March 2026 vs 3.21% in February 2026.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever quarterly revenue; YoY change not stated
Low tax charge: tax netted against refunds of INR788 crore in FY26, including INR330 crore in Q4
Crossed INR40,000 crore; double-digit growth in edible oil and FMCG

financial_highlights.value: INR2,890 crore, EBITDA INR292.16 crore, 10.11% margin

financial_highlights.metric: Oil palm plantation revenue / EBITDA (Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.value: INR1,793 crore revenue, INR357 crore EBITDA
financial_highlights.change: EBITDA vs INR203 crore in prior-year period (as stated on call)
Oil palm segment revenue of INR185 crore in Q4 cited in prepared remarks

qa_highlights.question: Biscuit category growth in Q4 FY26, whether it met expectations, and how the category is shaping up in April-May.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said biscuit growth was roughly 13% YoY (initially said over 15%, later corrected) and a marginal sequential dip from INR490 crore in Q3 to INR478 crore in Q4, attributed to seasonality and consumption disruption. Target remains high double-digit growth; Q1 FY27 expected to show a substantial uptick from INR478 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Foods revenue fall mid-teens YoY in Q4, and was there a one-off in the low tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Rice demand fell substantially through FY26, and ghee sales dropped about INR129 crore on early summer onset and Middle East disruption. Q4 tax was low because the company netted earlier-year refunds of INR788 crore in FY26, including INR330 crore in Q4, against current tax demand following post-CIRP assessment.

qa_highlights.question: Segment EBITDA for the quarter (Foods, biscuits, nutraceuticals, Nutrela, HPC).
qa_highlights.answer: Foods combined EBITDA INR72 crore (ethnic foods INR66 crore, staples INR5.46 crore); biscuits INR65 crore; nutraceuticals INR2 crore; Nutrela INR16.85 crore; HPC INR136 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Edible oil volumes for Q4 and FY26, and price hikes taken.
qa_highlights.answer: Edible oil volume 20.3 lakh tonnes vs 18.84 lakh tonnes; aggregate segment volume 25.1 lakh vs 23.64 lakh tonnes. Edible oil volume rose about 80,000 tonnes Q3 to Q4 and 1.5 lakh tonnes over FY25 to FY26. Oil price increases of 10-15% (about 14%) were passed through almost daily; staples up 2-5%, ghee repriced, other ethnic foods largely not repriced.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and higher borrowings: what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Extra customer credit of about INR700-800 crore was extended amid market conditions, and advances were paid to vendors to secure raw materials, raising borrowings. Management aims to collect receivables within one to two quarters and return to cash procurement if geopolitics permit.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 guidance for edible oil volume, Foods and HPC revenue and margins, and blended EBITDA.
qa_highlights.answer: Edible oil volume growth 3-5%, slightly below 4%. Foods revenue growth 8-10% blended, with Foods margin recovering to about 10%. HPC revenue growth about 15% with EBITDA margin 18%-plus, about 200 bps better than under the parent. Blended EBITDA growth 12-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Near-term impact of Indonesian palm oil export centralisation on edible oil revenue and margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the disruption to private trade creates short-term volatility but benefits large players holding inventory; Q1 and Q2 FY27 expected to be very positive for edible oil and oilseed crushing. Volume growth still tracks national consumption of about 3-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Palm oil plantation EBITDA for Q4 and FY26.
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 plantation revenue INR1,793 crore and EBITDA INR357 crore, vs INR203 crore prior year (a prior-year figure of INR1,262 crore was also cited, apparently a revenue number). Drivers: maturing plantations and higher palm oil prices.

risks_watch: Crude-linked edible oil price volatility and Indonesian export centralisation; management expects Q1-Q2 FY27 to benefit but the pass-through pattern and margin outcome are unproven.
Edible oil EBITDA margin of 2.58% in Q4 and FY26 against a 2-4% target range; consumer shift toward mustard oil could affect branded mix.
Foods weakness: rice demand decline, drought/El Nino and government policy risk for staples; ghee softness linked to Middle East disruption.
Working capital stress: receivable days up with INR700-800 crore extra credit to customers and higher borrowings from vendor advances; collection timeline is one to two quarters.
Biscuit growth slowed to about 13% YoY from over 15% in Q3 (per management correction); watch whether Q1 FY27 shows the promised uptick.
Low Q4 tax charge due to refunds of INR788 crore; PBT margin of 2.10% in Q4 means reported profit quality depends on one-time refund adjustments.
key_quotes: So, the overall market growth, I think we should be quite aligned to that.
I think we should see a good growth of anywhere between 12% to 15% growth for the next year.
But overall, the target that we continue to place for ourselves is upwards in high double digits.
Crude-linked volatility remains elevated, which would make the operating environment increasingly challenging for smaller and unorganized players.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on FY27 guidance and on the company's scale advantage over smaller players, while staying cautious on near-term staples, rice, ghee and input-cost pass-through. Answers were direct on volumes and segment EBITDA, but several figures had to be corrected on the call and some answers were deferred to the CFO.
